entries.summary: Bulletin ID: 2026-173-AWS Publication Date: 11/06/2026 09:00 AM PST Description: We identified CVE-2026-122193, an OS command injection issue in an example provided in the set-up documentation.
entries.text: Bulletin ID: 2026-173-AWS Publication Date: 11/06/2026 09:00 AM PST Description: We identified CVE-2026-122193, an OS command injection issue in an example provided in the set-up documentation. The example included a script that creates AWS Systems Manager (SSM) documents (Rex-RO and Rex-RW) for running scripts on managed instances. Due to how the example script handled input parameters, a user with permissions to invoke the SSM document could supply crafted input that would run unintended operating system commands on the managed instance, outside of the REX sandbox. The scriptArgs parameter is affected by the same class of issue. Impacted versions: This is not an issue in a shipped REX artifact version. Refer to the article below for the most up-to-date and complete information. Read this article
entries.title: CVE-2026-122193 - Issue with Trusted Remote Execution Setup Guide - OS command injection in the example SSM documents in Trusted Remote Execution (REX)

entries.text: Bulletin ID: 2026-174-AWS Publication Date: 11/09/2026 13:00 PM PST Description: AWS ParallelCluster CLI is an open source command line tool, distributed on PyPI as aws-parallelcluster. We identified CVE-2026-124033, an issue where the export-cluster-logs and export-image-logs commands in the AWS ParallelCluster CLI before version 3.16.0 contain a relative path traversal issue. An authenticated remote user with write access to the log export Amazon S3 bucket could use a crafted S3 object key to write files outside the intended export directory on the machine running the command. Impacted versions: >= 3.0.0 AND < 3.16.0 Refer to the article for the most up-to-date and complete information. Read this article
entries.title: CVE-2026-124033 - Relative path traversal in the log export commands in AWS ParallelCluster CLI

entries.text: Bulletin ID: 2026-176-AWS Publication Date: 11/10/2026 08:30 AM PST Description: We identified CVE-2026-125271 of AWS API MCP Server. The server normalized operation names incorrectly before comparing them to the operator ' s security policy, so operations whose names contain consecutive capital letters never matched a correctly written denyList or elicitList entry. This might allow an actor to execute AWS API operations that the operator's security policy was configured to deny or require elicitation for. Impacted versions: >= 0.2.13 AND < 1.5.1 Refer to the article for the most up-to-date and complete information.
entries.title: CVE-2026-125271 - AWS API MCP Server Security Policy Bypass via Incorrect Operation Name Normalization

entries.text: Bulletin ID: 2026-181-AWS Publication Date: 11/12/2026 13:00 PM PST Description: We identified CVE-2026-127119, an issue in the EMR module of AWS SDK for pandas (awswrangler) from version 1.1.0 before 3.18.0. When a cluster is created without an explicit log location, the library uses a predictable default S3 bucket name for the cluster logs without verifying that the caller's account owns that bucket. Impacted versions: >= 1.1.0 AND < 3.18.0 Refer to the article for the most up-to-date and complete information.

entries.text: Bulletin ID: 2026-190-AWS Publication Date: 11/19/2026 10:00 AM PST Description: AWS is aware of security releases that the PHP Foundation published on November 19, 2026. PHP versions 8.2.36, 8.3.37, 8.4.28, and 8.5.13 address 17 issues across the PHP 8.2, 8.3, 8.4, and 8.5 branches. The issues are in the following components: The PHP engine PHP-FPM and the PHP CGI binary The SOAP, Phar, session, DOM, and date extensions The HTTP and FTP stream wrappers The PHP 8.5 RFC 3986 URI implementation Patching the affected software remains the only complete fix and should be the first priority. We will update this bulletin as more information becomes available. Refer to the article for the most up-to-date and complete information.

entries.summary: Bulletin ID: 2026-191-AWS Publication Date: 11/19/2026 13:00 PM PST Description: We identified CVE-2026-132607, an issue in the decryption component of Amazon S3 Encryption Client for PHP in the AWS SDK for PHP.
entries.text: Bulletin ID: 2026-191-AWS Publication Date: 11/19/2026 13:00 PM PST Description: We identified CVE-2026-132607, an issue in the decryption component of Amazon S3 Encryption Client for PHP in the AWS SDK for PHP. The client did not verify the length of the AES-GCM authentication tag recorded in an object's metadata. A user with read and write access to an encrypted object, who knows or can guess its plaintext, might craft a ciphertext that decrypts to plaintext of their choice of the same length. This requires repeated writes to the object. The issue does not disclose the plaintext or the encryption key. Refer to the article for the most up-to-date and complete information.
entries.title: CVE-2026-132607 - GCM authentication tag length downgrade in Amazon S3 Encryption Client for PHP

entries.text: Bulletin ID: 2026-192-AWS Publication Date: 11/19/2026 15:00 PM PST Description: AWS is aware of the nginx issues published on November 18, 2026 (CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-123634, CVE-2026-113425, CVE-2026-121810 and CVE-2026-118899). These issues have been addressed in nginx version 1.30.7 (stable) and 1.31.9 (mainline). We recommend upgrading to the latest version. We are actively deploying mitigations worldwide to address these issues. Because these issues can be leveraged at the HTTP/2 protocol layer before a complete HTTP request is formed, AWS WAF managed and custom rules cannot effectively detect or block them. Refer to the article for the most up-to-date and complete information.
entries.title: Issue with nginx HTTP/2 Implementation

entries.summary: Bulletin ID: 2026-193-AWS Publication Date: 11/19/2026 15:05 PM PST Description: On November 18, 2026, the Ruby maintainers published fixes for seven issues in CRuby's regular expression engine and string case…
entries.text: Bulletin ID: 2026-193-AWS Publication Date: 11/19/2026 15:05 PM PST Description: On November 18, 2026, the Ruby maintainers published fixes for seven issues in CRuby's regular expression engine and string case conversion, including CVE-2026-132825. These issues affect Ruby versions before 4.0.10, 3.4.13, and 3.3.14 and could allow remote code execution in some configurations. These issues are memory-safety issues in Ruby's regular expression engine and in string case conversion on certain non-UTF-8 encodings. When an application processes third party-controlled input through these code paths, a remote, unauthenticated actor might be able to crash the process, read memory, or run arbitrary code. Applications built on Rack, including Rails and Sinatra, might be reachable through default request handling. Refer to the article for the most up-to-date and complete information.
entries.title: CVE-2026-132825 and related issues – Ruby regular expression engine and string case conversion

entries.summary: Bulletin ID: 2026-196-AWS Publication Date: 11/23/2026 12:00 PM PST Description: We identified CVE-2026-134056, an out-of-bounds write issue in AWS-LC's padded block cipher decryption.
entries.text: Bulletin ID: 2026-196-AWS Publication Date: 11/23/2026 12:00 PM PST Description: We identified CVE-2026-134056, an out-of-bounds write issue in AWS-LC's padded block cipher decryption. It affects applications that decrypt CBC or ECB ciphertext with PKCS7 padding over multiple update calls. If the output buffer is the minimum documented size, AWS-LC can write one byte past its end. This might crash the application or corrupt adjacent memory. This issue does not disclose data. The aws-lc-rs StreamingDecryptingKey API has a similar issue with cbc_pkcs7 and ecb_pkcs7. Its less_safe_update function can write up to one block (16 bytes for AES) past the buffer. Single-call decryption is not affected. Neither is decryption without padding, nor modes such as CTR, CFB, and GCM. Customers of AWS services do not need to take action. Refer to the article for the most up-to-date and complete information.
entries.title: CVE-2026-134056 - Out-of-bounds write in padded block cipher decryption in AWS-LC

entries.text: Bulletin ID: 2026-197-AWS Publication Date: 11/23/2026 13:30 PM PST Description: Amazon SSM Agent is the AWS Systems Manager agent that runs on EC2 instances so they can be managed through Systems Manager. We identified CVE-2026-134069, an issue in Amazon SSM Agent on AWS-provided Windows Server AMIs released before 2026-09-09, where instances launched from the same AMI shared one instance registration key. On instances managed through Default Host Management Configuration, a local user without administrative privileges might be able to obtain the instance's Default Host Management Configuration role credentials. Impacted versions: Amazon SSM Agent < 3.3.5226.0 on AWS Windows Server AMIs released before 2026-09-09. Instances launched from these AMIs remain affected after an in-place agent upgrade. Refer to the article for the most up-to-date and complete information.
entries.title: CVE-2026-134069 - Use of a default cryptographic key in the instance registration of Amazon SSM Agent on AWS Windows Server AMIs

Under certain circumstances, an authenticated database user with specific privileges might be able to execute arbitrary operating system commands as the database operating system user. entries.summary: Bulletin ID: 2026-199-AWS Publication Date: 11/24/2026 10:30 AM PST Description: Graph Explorer is an open-source tool for browsing and searching graph data, which customers self-host against Amazon Neptune or other…
entries.text: Bulletin ID: 2026-199-AWS Publication Date: 11/24/2026 10:30 AM PST Description: Graph Explorer is an open-source tool for browsing and searching graph data, which customers self-host against Amazon Neptune or other graph databases. We identified CVE-2026-134066, an issue in the query construction of Graph Explorer before version 3.2.1. Graph Explorer inserted property keys and labels read from the connected graph database into Gremlin, openCypher and SPARQL query text without escaping. A user with write access to the connected graph database could create a crafted property key or label that, when another user performs a search, causes Graph Explorer to run unintended query logic that accesses and modifies data in that database with Graph Explorer's privileges. On Amazon Neptune, the SPARQL path is not affected. Impacted versions: < 3.2.1 Refer to the article for the most up-to-date and complete information.
entries.title: CVE-2026-134066 - Query injection via schema-derived identifiers in Graph Explorer

entries.summary: Bulletin ID: 2026-200-AWS Publication Date: 11/24/2026 11:00 AM PST Description: Amazon ECS MCP Server is an open-source Model Context Protocol server that lets AI agents and assistants manage and troubleshoot Amazon…
entries.text: Bulletin ID: 2026-200-AWS Publication Date: 11/24/2026 11:00 AM PST Description: Amazon ECS MCP Server is an open-source Model Context Protocol server that lets AI agents and assistants manage and troubleshoot Amazon ECS workloads using the operator's AWS credentials. We identified CVE-2026-135614, an issue in the troubleshooting tool of the Amazon ECS MCP Server (awslabs.ecs-mcp-server) before 0.1.36. With the sensitive data setting at its default, the troubleshooting tool returned container environment variable values and secret references from ECS task definitions without the redaction the setting is intended to apply. This might allow a remote actor who can influence the agent's input, for example through prompt injection, to obtain those values. Impacted versions: < 0.1.36 Refer to the article for the most up-to-date and complete information.
entries.title: CVE-2026-135614 - Sensitive data redaction bypass in the troubleshooting tool in Amazon ECS MCP Server

entries.text: Bulletin ID: 2026-201-AWS Publication Date: 11/24/2026 11:15 AM PST Description: Amazon OpenSearch Service is a managed service for deploying, operating, and scaling OpenSearch clusters in the AWS Cloud. We identified CVE-2026-135414, an issue in snapshot repository registration in Amazon OpenSearch Service. A user with snapshot management permissions on a domain could set a repository endpoint that caused the domain's service-operated nodes to send requests to network destinations that the user specified. This issue is addressed in service software R20260720. We recommend that customers update their domains to R20260720 or later. Impacted versions: Amazon OpenSearch Service service software before R20260720 Refer to the article for the most up-to-date and complete information.
entries.title: CVE-2026-135414 - Server-side request forgery in snapshot repository registration in Amazon OpenSearch Service

entries.text: Bulletin ID: 2026-202-AWS Publication Date: 11/25/2026 09:00 AM PST Description: Kiro Web is a cloud-hosted, AI-powered integrated development environment where subscribers use AI agents to work on software development tasks in the browser. We are aware of CVE-2026-136267, an issue in Kiro Web where tool-call markup inside content an agent session read, such as a repository file or a web page, could be repeated by certain models and run as a command in the subscriber's hosted development environment without a consent prompt. The issue affected agent sessions using DeepSeek v3.2, GLM-5, MiniMax M2.1, MiniMax M2.5, or Qwen3-coder-next from 2026-05-18 through 2026-10-30. Impacted versions: Kiro Web before 2026-10-30 Refer to the article for the most up-to-date and complete information.
entries.title: CVE-2026-136267 - Improper neutralization of special elements used in an OS command in Kiro Web

entries.text: Bulletin ID: 2026-203-AWS Publication Date: 11/25/2026 11:30 AM PST Description: AWS Systems Manager Automation provides AWS-managed runbooks that customers can run directly or through integrations such as AWS Config remediation. Session Manager, a capability of AWS Systems Manager, stores each account's regional session preferences in the SSM-SessionManagerRunShell document. We identified CVE-2026-134070, where improper input validation in the AWS-managed AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook AWSConfigRemediation-EnableSystemsManagerSessionManagerAuditLogsToS3 might allow an authenticated remote user who is permitted to run the runbook to set unintended configuration in the account's Regional Session Manager preferences document (SSM-SessionManagerRunShell) via a crafted S3KeyPrefix parameter value. This applies only when that document does not already exist in the Region. The unintended configuration can include arbitrary commands, which then run on managed instances when other users start Session Manager sessions. Impacted versions: Revisions created before 2026-10-22 (UTC) Refer to the article for the most up-to-date and complete information.
entries.title: CVE-2026-134070 - Improper input sanitization in the AWS Config remediation runbook AWSConfigRemediation-EnableSystemsManagerSessionManagerAuditLogsToS3
